traits.notes: The seedling exhibits a whorled leaf arrangement with 5-6 elliptic, entire, shiny leaves per node. The leaves are simple, with pinnate venation and short petioles. The stem is young and woody, green to brown, with no visible trichomes, latex, or stipules. One leaf shows white vein patterns, possibly from a leaf miner, but no other damage is clearly visible. The pink tag is an artificial marker and not part of the plant. All observations are based on multiple images showing the same individual from different angles.

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves clearly attached at the same node, visible in close-up images, with 5-6 leaves radiating from a single point)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely at the shoot apex, forming a whorled rosette)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf has a single blade without leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin with no teeth or serrations visible)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broadest near the middle, tapering to both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is gently curved, not tapering or heart-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex, with secondary veins branching off laterally)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins clearly visible, running parallel to each other and close together)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny, glabrous (surface appears smooth and glossy, no visible hairs)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible surface hairs or fuzz)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is relatively short compared to leaf blade, less than 1/5 the leaf length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (circular in cross-section, no wings or grooves visible)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm, slightly rough, and brownish, typical of young woody stems)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: green to brown (young stems are green, older portions are brownish)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no structures observed at leaf base that resemble stipules)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate visible on stem or leaves)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base visible; not applicable as leaf not compound)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)

F. Notes: The seedling exhibits a whorled leaf arrangement with 5-6 elliptic, entire, shiny leaves per node. The leaves are simple, with pinnate venation and short petioles. The stem is young and woody, green to brown, with no visible trichomes, latex, or stipules. One leaf shows white vein patterns, possibly from a leaf miner, but no other damage is clearly visible. The pink tag is an artificial marker and not part of the plant. All observations are based on multiple images showing the same individual from different angles.
